items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to fiscal intermediaries in the consumer directed personal assistance program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5565

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to fiscal interme-
diaries in the consumer directed personal assistance program

PURPOSE:

This bill defines fiscal intermediary services, within the consumer
directed personal assistance program, and requires that fiscal interme-
diaries providing such services be licensed by the Commissioner of
Health.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill defines the terms "fiscal intermediary" and
"fiscal intermediary services" and specifies that no entity provide
fiscal intermediary services without a license issued by the Commission-
er of Health. It then details the process for becoming a licensed fiscal
intermediary and establishes a fee of $2,000.

Section 2 provides an effective date.

EXISTING LAW:

Section 365-f, the consumer directed personal assistance program,
currently provides No specific guidelines as to who can be a fiscal
intermediary.

JUSTIFICATION:

The consumer directed personal assistance program is intended to permit
chronically ill and/or physically disabled individuals receiving home
care services under the medical assistance program greater flexibility
and freedom of choice in obtaining such services.  In 1997, when the
program became law, it was left to the local departments' of social
services to decide with whom they would contract to provide the fiscal
intermediary services. At the time, the program was small and aimed at a
specific group of individuals.  There was not much demand and, general-
ly, providers were not looking to offer the service. With the shift to
managed care and managed long term care, the program has been growing
tremendously, experiencing approximately 50% growth rate from 2012 to
the end of 2014.

As agencies see this growth, they have looked to enter the CDPA market-
place, often with little to no understanding of the program.  Indeed,
the Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program remains one of the
only industries in health care that is not regulated or licensed in any
manner. In an effort to ensure that public Medicaid dollars are spent
effectively and efficiently, and fiscal intermediaries are operating the
program in a manner consistent with state laws and regulations while

taking adequate steps to ensure quality services and prevent fraud, it
is necessary to license these entities and provide a level of oversight
while still protecting the unique nature of the program.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No cost to the state, as the fees associated with licensure are meant to
offset any costs.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

The first day of July after it shall have become law; provided effective
immediately the commissioner shall make regulations and take action to
implement the law on that date.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 302

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Senate Bill Number 5565-B, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  social services law, in relation to fiscal
      intermediaries  in  the  consumer  directed  personal   assistance
      program"

    NOT APPROVED

  This bill would provide for licensure of fiscal intermediaries operat-
ing  in  the  State's  consumer  directed  personal  assistance  program
(CDPAP).

  I strongly support the CDPAP initiative,  as  it  facilitates  persons
with  disabilities  having  decision-making power, and control over, the
home health care they receive.  I  also  recognize  that  ensuring  that
fiscal  intermediaries  act in a responsible manner is critically impor-
tant. To that end, the Department of Health  (Department)  requires  all
fiscal  intermediaries  to obtain a Medicaid number, thus subjecting the
entities to additional oversight by the federal government, the  Depart-
ment,  and  the Office of Medicaid Inspector General. The Department has
also increased its oversight of managed long term care plans (MLTCP)  to
clarify  the  conditions under which an MLTCP may sign an administrative
agreement with a  fiscal  intermediary  to  administer  CDPAP  services,
including  the  fiscal  intermediary's  agreement  to  meet  all  of the
requirements as outlined in the CDPAP regulations at  18  NYCRR  Section
505.28.

  The  next step toward ensuring that all fiscal intermediaries are held
to the same compliance standard is to develop a statewide regulatory and
licensure program. However, the statewide licensure program proposed  by
this  bill  poses  significant fiscal challenges which must be carefully
evaluated and negotiated as part of the  budgeting  process.  For  these
reasons,  I am constrained to veto this bill. In the interim, however, I
am directing the Department to work collaboratively with the  Department
of  Financial Services, the bill's sponsors, and interested stakeholders
to develop a fiscally-sound framework  for  regulating  fiscal  interme-
diaries that best serves the needs of persons utilizing CDPAP.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
